root_idea.summary: The root has several divergent lexical branches rather than one securely unifying derivational principle. A prominent branch concerns forceful impact or spreading, extended from bodily action to forceful speech.
root_idea.development: Alongside the forceful-action branch reflected in Quranic speech, the lexical record preserves independent branches for laying down, marking or abrading, cooking, terrain, natural disposition, animals, and medical conditions.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form سَلَقَ rather than the inflected QAC surface identity سَلَقُ.

senses.definition: To assail or hurt forcefully with the tongue; to address someone harshly or vehemently.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction سَلَقُوكُمْ بِأَلْسِنَةٍ حِدَادٍ, the force is verbal assault or smiting with sharp tongues. The physical sense of striking is a related Classical usage, not the required object of this construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To throw someone down on the back or back of the neck; to prostrate or extend someone on the back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of a physician extending a person on the back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lay a woman down and have sexual intercourse with her; to spread and compress her while so laid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specific transitive construction referring to laying the woman on her back; the lexical evidence does not impose a narrower age or social-status restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To thrust or pierce, push back, repel, dash against, or strike forcefully.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the physical-impact branch of the verb and its verbal noun, distinct from the Quranic tongue-based construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of feet or hoofs, to mark or make tracks upon a road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional intransitive use with feet, hoofs, or similar means of marking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To abrade or strip a surface: to flay with a whip, gall skin, abrade a rider’s thigh, peel flesh from bone, or remove hair or fur with hot water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The objects and means vary by construction; these are related surface-removal and abrasion uses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To boil or cook with water, especially herbs, leguminous plants, eggs, or other food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb can describe slight boiling, boiling merely in water, or cooking with hot water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of cold, to nip, shrivel, or blast herbage and plants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use in which cold damages vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To oil or grease a leather water-bag or hide; to smear a camel with tar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of treating leather or an animal’s surface with an oily or coating substance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fasten a sack by inserting one loop into the other, or inserting the stick into the loop.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical packing construction used with the loops of a جوالق or related sacks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pustular, scaling, excoriative, or roughened condition affecting the tongue, mouth, teeth-roots, or eyelids.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the mouth it may involve pimples or scaling at the roots of the teeth; in the eye it involves roughness and redness of the eyelids, sometimes with loss of eyelashes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Innate nature, natural disposition, or constitution.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used in the phrase هٰذِهِ الَّتِي سُلِقَ عَلَيْهَا, referring to the constitution or disposition to which someone is naturally adapted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To call out, cry out, shout, or raise the voice vehemently, especially in grief or calamity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive use; one attributed alternative explains the verbal noun as a woman’s slapping and scratching her face in mourning, while the vehement-shouting explanation is preferred in the cited discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To run.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An additional intransitive use, as in سَلَقَ سَلْقَةً, “he ran a run.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a man’s camel, to become white-backed after the healing of galls.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV intransitive use describing the healed and whitened back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hunt, snare, or trap a she-wolf.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV transitive use with a she-wolf as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become restless, agitated, or in a state of commotion on one’s bed because of anxiety or pain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This use is reported with س; one cited authority says that the better-known form in this sense is with ص.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ascend, climb, or scale a wall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V construction with a wall or similar smooth vertical surface as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the tongue, to become affected with an excoriation; of the eye, to develop the associated redness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VII medical use connected with the condition called سُلَاق.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lie or sleep on one’s back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A special derived form, compared in the lexical discussion with اِسْتَلْقَى.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A scar or mark left by a healed gall or sore, or by a strap on a camel; also a track or mark made on a road by feet or hoofs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun covers marks on an animal’s back or side as well as impressed tracks and similar marks on the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Beet or a related edible herb or plant, especially one whose leaves are cooked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plant name with several reported regional or etymological explanations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wolf, especially a she-wolf.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term’s gender application is debated in the lexical evidence. The wolf also supplies the comparison in descriptions of a clamorous or overpowering person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A clamorous, long-tongued, vehement, foul, evil, or lewd woman, by comparison with a she-wolf.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application of the animal term to a woman’s speech or conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female lizard of the ضَبّ kind, or a female locust after laying her eggs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two animal applications are reported as lexical uses of the same feminine form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A watercourse or channel through which water flows between elevated or rugged tracts; also an even depressed tract of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The terrain sense has several plural forms and overlaps lexically with related lowland terms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An even or smooth plain, especially a low tract of good soil or land producing herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical noun; some descriptions specify a treeless depressed plain or meadow-like lowland.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mode or act of compressing someone upon the back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun related to the construction of laying someone on the back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Leaves or other plant matter that have fallen from trees or shrubs, or vegetation dried and parched by sun or weather.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may refer either to fallen leaves or to plant matter affected by heat or cold.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Honey or a substance built lengthwise by bees along the hive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized beekeeping term with variant explanations of the material fabricated by the bees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The side of a road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two sides of a road may be called سَلِيقَا الطَّرِيقِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Food cooked with water, especially herbs or leguminous plants; also bruised millet cooked with milk or a related famine food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A food noun derived from the cooking sense; the reported preparations and ingredients vary by usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place where a camel’s breast-girth strap emerges at the side, or the strips of flesh between the sides.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical or harness-related noun with more than one reported explanation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A Salūqī hunting dog or a type of coat of mail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nisbah term whose application to dogs and armor is variously related to place names in the lexical record.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Reportedly, a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This sense is uncertain: the cited verse is reported to be mistranscribed, leaving the orthography and explanation doubtful.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Natural, untaught speech or a dialect spoken freely according to native habit rather than learned grammatical usage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can describe speech that is chaste and eloquent in vocabulary while irregular in inflection, or a speaker’s native desert dialect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sitting-place of a ship’s captain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nautical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A Christian festival commemorating the Ascension of Jesus into Heaven.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is reported as foreign or Syriac Arabicized and is linked by derivational explanation to climbing a wall.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who raises her voice in a calamity or at someone’s death, or who slaps her face in mourning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The preferred explanation concerns loud wailing; the face-slapping description is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quick or swift; especially a she-camel with penetrating energy in her pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine epithet applied to a she-camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The upper interior parts of the mouth, near the uvula and where the tongue rises.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as a plural form with no ordinary singular in this application.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An eloquent, forceful speaker or orator; also a sharp, cutting, or eloquent tongue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative active-participant noun emphasizing vehemence of voice or speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A skinned fowl cooked or boiled in water by itself; by extension, boiled meat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical record marks this as a colloquial or vulgar term in some usage.

cautions: The QAC surface سَلَقُ is an inflected Quranic form with an attached pronoun; the public citation form is normalized to سَلَقَ.
The root contains several lexically divergent branches, so shared consonants should not be taken as proof of a single direct meaning.
The reported sword sense of سَلُوقِيّ is uncertain because the cited verse is said to be mistranscribed.
The restless-bed sense of تَسَلَّقَ is reported with س, while one cited authority identifies the better-known form in that sense with ص.
